newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma rules out talks with Aung San Suu Kyi.
newsitem.headline: Burma rules out talks with Aung San Suu Kyi.

text.p: A founding member of Burma's 20-member military State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) ruled out on Monday any talks with opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi, saying she "will always be against us".
"She will always be against us...at this time, it is impossible (to hold dialogue with her)," Lieutenant-General Kyaw Ba, minister of hotels and tourism, told Reuters in an interview.
The minister said talks with political parties over a future government would only be held after a new national constitution was drafted and the nation's economy had improved.

In November 1995 Suu Kyi pulled her National League for Democracy (NLD) out of a government-organised National Convention which has been drawing up a new constitution in discussion with various ethnic groups and parties.
The withdrawal angered the SLORC which has refused to hold any formal discussions with the Nobel laureate and has prevented her and the NLD from actively carrying out political activities.
Kyaw Ba said many improvements would have to be made and unity among ethnic groups achieved before the army would devise a way to share power. He did not give any timeframe for this.
